transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess… it’s my eating. Sometimes when I’m alone in the kitchen and I start, it feels like I can’t really stop, even though I’m telling myself to put it away. It scares me a bit.
How do you feel after one of these episodes of eating when you couldn't stop?

I feel pretty ashamed afterward. Like… I’ll look at what I ate and think I wasted food that was meant for everyone, and that I’m too old to be doing this. I usually just sit there feeling awful and tell myself it won’t happen again.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating during those episodes?
No… not really. Once I start, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, it’s like I sort of step aside. I’m telling myself, “Janet, put it away,” but I just… don’t.
Do you ever try to make up for what you've eaten during one of these episodes by doing something to counteract it?
Um… I’m not sure what you mean by counteract it. I don’t really have anything specific I can think of. I mostly just feel bad afterward.
Do you ever try to vomit or get rid of what you've eaten after one of these episodes?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I feel terrible after, but I don’t try to make myself throw up or anything like that.
How often do these episodes of eating when you couldn't stop happen?
I guess… most weeks. I looked back at my kitchen calendar and it’s usually once, sometimes twice in a week. It’s been like that for months now.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping close track… my clothes maybe feel a little different sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s significant.
Do you feel guilty during the episodes of eating when you couldn't stop, or is the guilt something you feel afterward?

It’s more afterward, I think. During it I’m just… not really thinking. Then after, I feel awful about myself, ashamed. Like I wasted food I meant to share, and I tell myself I’m too old to be doing this and that it won’t happen again.
Do you ever exercise more than usual after one of these episodes to try to burn off the calories?
Not really. I mean… I don’t think I do that. I might feel bad afterward, but I’m not usually going out to exercise because of it.
Have these episodes of eating when you couldn't stop been happening for more than 3 months?
Yeah… it’s been more than 3 months. Probably about a year or so now. It started after my close friend from the food bank died… maybe a year and two months ago.
Have you experienced any significant weight gain or loss since these episodes started?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping close track of my weight. My clothes maybe feel a little different sometimes, but… I don’t know if it’s significant.
Do you think these episodes where you eat and can't stop are usually followed by any behaviors intended to prevent weight gain?
I don’t think so… not anything on purpose like that. I just usually feel bad and try to move on, I guess.
Do you ever use laxatives or diuretics after eating?
No… I don’t use things like that after eating.
Do you ever fast or severely restrict your food intake after one of these episodes of eating when you couldn't stop?
I don’t really fast, no. I might eat less for a bit if I feel uncomfortable, but I don’t think I severely restrict on purpose.
During these episodes where you can't stop eating, do you think you're eating a lot more food than most people would eat under the same circumstances?

Yeah… I think so. Like, some afternoons after I’ve been at the food bank or baking for a senior-center thing, I’ll come home and have leftovers, then banana bread, chips, cheese, cookies… and afterward it’s just clear it was more than I’d ever put on a plate for someone else.
On average, how many times a month would you say you have one of these episodes where you eat and can't stop?

Um… I looked back at my kitchen calendar, and with the food bank weeks and all, it’s been most weeks. Maybe once or twice a week, so… I guess around four to eight times a month. It’s been that way for many months.
Do you feel like you're completely unable to control how much you're eating during these episodes?
Yes… that’s what scares me. Once I start, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, it feels like I can’t get myself to stop. I’ll be telling myself, “Janet, put it away,” but I just… don’t.
Do you ever do anything to try to make up for the amount you ate during these episodes, like exercising a lot or skipping meals the next day?
I don’t really know… I haven’t kept track of doing anything like that. I might eat lighter after, but I don’t think of it as, um, making up for it exactly.
Have you ever done anything to try to make up for the amount you ate during these episodes, such as purging, using laxatives, or excessive exercise?
I… I don’t think so. Not like that. I haven’t really done those things, at least not that I can say for sure.
